samples.prompt: Write a philosophical essay contrasting two modes of reasoning: one that begins with first principles and fundamental purposes, and another that starts with immediate observations and works backward. Use an extended metaphor involving a common object to illustrate the difference between these approaches.
samples.generated:
The two modes of reasoning I am going to contrast in this essay are, on the one hand, those which begin with first principles and fundamental purposes, and, on the other hand, those which start with immediate observations and work backward.
I have chosen a pair of shoes as an illustration. Let us suppose that the philosopher who reasons from first principles starts by saying:
```
All things that are real are either God or matter.
Matter is something that is changeable.
Change is only possible where there is a change of place or position.
Change of place is only possible where there is motion.

Therefore the things that are real are either God or something that
is moving.

God does not move; therefore all that is real must be a moving thing.
Every moving thing is a living thing.
Therefore every thing that is real is a living thing.
```

Let us suppose that the philosopher who reasons from immediate observations starts by saying:
```
This shoe has been worn once.

That shoe has been worn twice.
```

Therefore it will have to be worn three times before it is worn as much as this shoe was worn once.

samples.prompt: Write a personal essay that revisits a place from your past, comparing how it appears now with your memories of it from years ago.
samples.generated:
It was a very long time ago, but I remember when I first saw the house in which my father had lived in his youth, and I have always loved to go back to it. It is a small house with a garden and a garden shed. The house itself looks like something out of a picture-book, and yet it is true. It is a house with a green shut-eye, and in front of the house there are a few trees and some bushes, with a few flower-beds between them. The garden sheds are the things that make a garden look like a garden; the garden itself is a thing of beauty only if these little sheds are there; they do not look like anything except a garden.

The house has been empty for many years; and now it has been emptied again by the removal of one more inhabitant, who went away last year. He had a wife and two children; and when he left the house I heard him say “I never shall see this house again.” That was the most terrible thing that could happen, that I should be deprived of the right to remember things as I remembered them. For we all live in our memories; and even though our own lives may pass before us, we find it hard to believe that our own minds shall not pass before them.
